previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, type 1 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted after developing fever and chills during dialysis, progressing to septic shock. She presented with altered mental status and was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and stress-dose steroids. Blood cultures grew E. coli, and given concern for dialysis catheter-related infection, the existing tunneled catheter was removed and a new one placed. Antibiotics were initially given with meropenem, then switched to ceftazidime based on sensitivities and to avoid nephrotoxicity, despite a history of cephalosporin-related neutropenia; CBC monitoring was initiated. Her symptoms resolved with treatment and dialysis. Imaging showed severe mitral regurgitation and mild pulmonary edema, managed supportively. She remained afebrile, with negative repeat blood cultures, and was discharged to extended care on a two-week course of ceftazidime with dialysis and close CBC monitoring.
problems: Septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli]
Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
Combined systolic and diastolic heart failure, unspecified
Cephalosporin group causing adverse effects in therapeutic use

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ yo F with PMH type 1 IDDM (s/p revision renal 
and pancreas transplants, ___ and ___, chronic diastolic and 
systolic CHF (Echo 35-40%, ___, recurrent MDR E coli UTIs, 
on dialysis for refractory hyperkalemia, initially presented 
with ___ lower extremity cellulitis s/p completed course of 
Vancomycin, sent to MICU for tachycardia, fevers, and 
respiratory distress requiring biPAP. She responded well to 
broad spectrum antibiotics and HD/ultrafiltration for fluid 
overload and transfered afebrile on room air.
.  
ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Low grade fevers:  After being on the floor for treatment of 
___ lower extremity DVT versus cellulitis (see below), she 
developed low grade fevers and tachycardia.  She was transferred 
to the ICU for further management of suspected pneumonia and 
evolving sepsis.  Due to her chronic immunosuppression and 
suspicious chest xray, her antibiotics were broadened to 
daptomycin, meropenem, and atovaquone.  She was fluid 
resuscitated judiciously to avoid volume overload given her 
heart failure and renal failure.  Beta glucan and galactomannans 
were sent and are still pending. Infectious disease consulted 
and felt this was not likely infectious process and antibiotics 
were narrowed to Meropenem for ___ompleted on 
___
.
# Respiratory distress: On floor patient developed progressive 
worsening respiratory status with increased work of breathing 
and developed hypoxia with exertion. Respiratory status 
initially improved with ultrafiltration but then she 
deteriorated exhibiting posturing, accessory muscle use and 
began tiring out and so she was transferred to MICU. Prior to 
transfer she was given 60mg IV Lasix x2 and started on braod 
spectrum antibiotics for HCAP coverage without improvement in 
her symptoms. While in the ICU, the patient was continued on 
antibiotics for possible pneumonia, but CXRs were more 
consistent with volume overload.  The patient's oxygen 
requirement increased in the unit, and she was using BIPAP.  She 
then underwent HD, which she tolerated very well.  Post HD, the 
patient's oxygen requirment dropped, and she was initially 
stable on ___ NC, and on transfer out of the unit, she was 
stable on RA.  The patient was also being followed by ID in the 
unit and her antibiotic coverage was reduced to ___, as 
atovaquone and dapto were discontinued.  As per ID recs, the 
Vanc was discontinued on D10 of treatment, and her ___ was 
continued.  Of note, the patient has a history sleep disordered 
breathing and has been tried on CPAP at home. She was called out 
to the floor with CPAP settings for overnight.   
.
# Tachycardia:  The patient became tachycardic, with rhythm in 
atrial fibrillation vs. atrial flutter.  The patient's pressure 
dropped into the ___ systolic during this episode of 
tachycardia, likely because of inadequate time for diastolic 
filling.  Amiodarone drip was started (1.0 mg/min for 6 hours, 
0.5 mg/min for 18 hours), and then she was maintained on 200 mg 
PO daily.  After starting the amiodarone, the patient's heart 
rates were better controlled and she remained hemodynamically 
stable. Coumadin was started and continued for atrial 
fibrillation anticoagulation.  
     
# ___ lower extremity suspected deep veinous thrombosis: 
Patient admitted with ___ non-occlusive popliteal DVT and was 
started on warfarin. However, the final read of her LENIs found 
that there was no DVT, and her warfarin was stopped after she 
had some episodes of hemoptysis in the ICU. She remained 
hemodynamically stable, with minimal pain, and no evidence of 
pulmonary embolism. Hemoptysis resolved.  
.
# Lower extremity erythema: Erythema marked on admission, 
thought to be due to DVT initially but then as above more likely 
isolated cellulitis. Cellulitis improved on Vancomycin however 
she continued to have fevers so was changed to daptomycin when 
she was transferred to the ICU. Erythema and swelling resolved 
with completion of antibiotics and hemodialysis to remove volume 
overload.
.

___ LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION: ___ year old woman with pneumonia, needing IV antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient. A pre procedure timeout and huddle
was performed per ___ protocol.

RADIOLOGIST: Dr. ___ (fellow) and Dr ___ (attending
radiologist) performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE: Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right brachial
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access. A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guide wire. The guidewire could not be advanced distal to brachiocephalic
vein. Through the peelaway sheath 10cc of Optiray 320 was injected. The
venogram demonstrated full occlusion at the right brachiocephalic vein. A
combination of ___ Kumpe catheter and a glidewire was used in attempt to cross
the occlusion, but it was unsuccessful. The case was discussed on the phone by
Dr ___ radiologist with Dr ___ attending and a
decision was made to place a midline line. Therefore, a double lumen midline
measuring 20 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with
its tip positioned 4 cm proximal to obstruction in the brachiocephalic vein
under fluoroscopic guidance. Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guide wire were then removed. The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION: 
1) Complete occlusion at the right brachiocephalic vein with multiple
collateral veins. 
2) Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided double lumen midline
placement via the right brachial venous approach. Final internal length is 20
cm, with the tip positioned in the subclavian vein. The line is ready to use.

HISTORY:  Transplant with respiratory distress.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with the study of ___, there is continued diffuse
bilateral pulmonary opacifications consistent with worsening effusions, volume
loss, and increased pulmonary vascular congestion.  Possibility of supervening
pneumonia must be seriously considered in the appropriate clinical setting,
though this is difficult to evaluate in view of the substrate of extensive
pulmonary changes.

Previous severe pulmonary edema has cleared with residual moderate right and

INDICATION:  Status post renal transplant and pancreatic transplant with
multiple intubations resulting in vocal cord dysfunction.

SWALLOWING VIDEO FLUOROSCOPY:  Oropharyngeal swallowing videofluoroscopy was
performed in conjunction with the speech and swallow division.  Multiple
consistencies of barium were administered.  Barium passed through the
oropharynx without evidence of obstruction.  A 13-mm barium tablet
demonstrated a slight holdup at the upper esophageal sphincter and even
further delay at the lower esophageal sphincter.  Multiple swallows of thin
barium were required to pass the tablet into the stomach.  There was no gross
aspiration or penetration seen.  Normal vocal cord function was observed.

IMPRESSION:  No gross aspiration or penetration seen.  Delayed passage of
13-mm tablet at the lower esophageal sphincter.  For full details, please
refer to the speech and swallow note in OMR.
